package_info.why_malicious: The affected versions of the Spring Core (spring-beans) package are vulnerable to remote code execution (RCE) due to improper handling of HTTP POST request parameters during data binding. Attackers can exploit this flaw to manipulate the ClassLoader and execute arbitrary code on servers running JRE 9+ and Tomcat 9+.

execution_context.trigger: At HTTP POST request processing time
execution_context.file_location: org.springframework.beans.BeanWrapperImpl (data binding logic within Spring Core)
required_permissions: Ability to send HTTP requests to the application

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
POST /vulnerable-endpoint HTTP/1.1
Host: vulnerable-server
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

class.module.classLoader[<payload>]=<malicious_value>
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At HTTP POST request processing time, the data binding logic in Spring Core interprets specially crafted request parameters (e.g., class.module.classLoader), allowing attacker-supplied values to be injected into internal Java objects, resulting in arbitrary code execution on the server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Allowing external HTTP request parameters to directly manipulate internal Java objects such as the ClassLoader is highly abnormal and dangerous, as it enables attackers to inject and execute arbitrary code remotely.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Spring applications should only map HTTP request parameters to simple POJO fields for safe data binding. They should never allow external input to alter the ClassLoader or internal Java runtime state, nor permit code execution as a result of data binding.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use of Spring's data binding is limited to mapping user input to application-defined data models (POJOs), not for accessing or modifying internal Java classes or runtime structures.
key_indicators: Presence of HTTP parameters targeting class.module.classLoader or similar internal Java properties
Data binding logic processing parameters that reference Java class loader or module internals
Execution of attacker-supplied code as a result of HTTP POST request processing
Exploitability limited to environments running JRE 9+ and Tomcat 9+

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a specially crafted HTTP POST request with parameters such as class.module.classLoader to a vulnerable Spring application endpoint.
attack_chain.leads_to: The request is processed by the Spring Core data binding logic, which interprets the malicious parameters.

attack_chain.action: Spring's data binding mechanism uses the malicious parameters to manipulate internal Java objects, specifically the ClassLoader.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary code is loaded and executed on the server, resulting in remote code execution (RCE).

behavioral_signatures: HTTP POST requests containing parameters such as class.module.classLoader or other references to internal Java classes
Unexpected manipulation of ClassLoader or internal Java objects via HTTP request parameters
Unusual or unauthorized code execution triggered during HTTP POST request processing
Abnormal data binding activity resulting in class or resource loading outside of normal application logic
file_indicators: No specific file indicators, as the exploit operates entirely in-memory within the Spring Core data binding logic
network_indicators: Inbound HTTP POST requests with suspicious or non-standard parameters targeting Spring-based endpoints, especially those referencing class.module.classLoader or similar internal Java properties
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor HTTP POST requests for parameters that attempt to access or modify internal Java classes (e.g., class.module.classLoader). Inspect application logs and stack traces for evidence of abnormal data binding activity or class/resource manipulation. Use updated vulnerability scanners to identify affected Spring Core versions. Monitor for unexpected code execution, process spawning, or anomalous behavior in Java applications running on JRE 9+ and Tomcat 9+.
